title: Order Granting Motion for Witnesses to Appear Remotely (Docket No. 26-035-05)
text:
- BEFORE THE PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION OF UTAH - 

Application of Rocky Mountain Power for 
Approval of a Large-Load Service 
Contract Between PacifiCorp and a 
Large-Load Customer 

DOCKET NO. 26-035-05 

ORDER GRANTING MOTION FOR 
WITNESSES TO APPEAR REMOTELY 

ISSUED: March 16, 2026 

On March 13, 2026, Rocky Mountain Power (RMP) filed its Settlement 
Stipulation along with its Motion Requesting Leave for Witness to Appear 
Telephonically at the hearing scheduled for March 17, 20261 in this docket (“Motion”). 
Specifically, RMP seeks permission from the Public Service Commission (PSC) 
allowing RMP’s witnesses, Ramon Mitchell and Robert Burns, to appear remotely at 
the hearing. RMP states its witness, Craig Eller, is expected to participate at the 
hearing in person. RMP further states it has contacted counsel for the Division of 
Public Utilities, the Office of Consumer Services, the Utah Association of Energy Users, 
and Utah Clean Energy, and that each has indicated it has no objection to RMP’s 
Motion. 
The PSC generally works to accommodate remote participation of non-local 
witnesses in recognition that it is significantly more convenient and less costly. The 
PSC prefers that testifying witnesses be present in the hearing room. Our preference 
is based on our experience that the technology being used to facilitate a witness’ 
remote participation may not, among other things, adequately allow an opportunity to 
appreciate that witness’ demeanor, or to facilitate rigorous questioning, and the

technology itself may present its own set of challenges and often provides a witness’ 
presentation far inferior to in-person testimony. Moreover, a witness’ remote 
participation can prove very challenging for the court reporter to accurately capture 
the testimony of that remote witness, which in turn can negatively affect the quality of 
the transcript of the proceeding. Thus, allowing the remote participation of witnesses 
in PSC proceedings is the exception, not the rule. 
We will, however, make an exception to our preference here based, in part, on 
the representation made by RMP that it is authorized to represent that all parties to 
this docket do not oppose the request made in the Motion. However, as a condition of 
granting the Motion, and to aid the PSC and the court reporter, if RMP chooses to have 
Mr. Mitchell and Mr. Burns participate remotely in the hearing, RMP must submit to 
the PSC before 5:00 pm on Monday, March 16, 2026, a copy of the written summary 
that Mr. Mitchell and Mr. Burns will use in providing their direct testimony. 
Accordingly, and subject to the foregoing condition, good cause exists and the 
Motion is granted.
